title: Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol third: foundation rotten — blessed angels elected, damned angels passed over, not from foresight of merits/rebellion but from mere liberty of will
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly, the very foundation upon which this whole argumentation leans is rotten: For it seems to take as granted that the Devils were reprobated from foresight of their actual sins. But we on the contrary say that the blessed Angels before the foundations of the world were laid were elected, not from their foresighted merits, but from the pure grace of the electing One; and that the damned Angels were likewise from eternity passed by, non-elect, or reprobated, not from foresight of future rebellion and of final hardening in the same, but from the mere will or liberty of God not willing to give them this grace. If therefore the Arminians from the reprobation of the Devils wish to prove that men were by no means reprobated except from antecedent foresight and consideration of actual sins, they ought first to have confirmed this by some solid argument as to the reprobation of the demons, before inferring thence consequences concerning the reprobation of men.
pass_b_english: Third: the very foundation this whole argument leans on is rotten. It seems to take as granted that the Devils were reprobated from foresight of their actual sins. We say the contrary: the blessed angels were elected before the world's foundations were laid — not from foresighted merits but from the electing One's pure grace; and the damned angels were likewise from eternity passed by, non-elect, or reprobated — not from foresight of future rebellion and final hardening in it, but from God's mere will or liberty not willing to give them that grace. So if Arminians from the Devils' reprobation want to prove men were reprobated only from antecedent foresight of actual sins, they ought first to confirm that by solid argument for the demons' reprobation before drawing consequences about men's.
source_text: Tertio, ipsum fundamentum cui innititur tota haec argumentatio putridum est: Nam videtur pro concesso sumere, Diabolos fuisse ex praevisione actualium suorum peccatorum reprobatos. At nos e contra dicimus, Angelos beatos ante jacta mundi fundamenta fuisse electos, non ex praevisis eorundem meritis, sed ex pura gratia eligentis; et Angelos damnatos fuisse pariter ab aeterno praeteritos, non-electos, sive reprobatos, non ex praevisione futurae rebellionis et finalis in eadem obdurationis, sed ex mera voluntate sive libertate Dei hanc gratiam illis donare nolentis. Si igitur Arminiani a Diabolorum reprobatione probare volunt homines minime fuisse reprobatos, nisi ex antecedente praevisione et consideratione actualium peccatorum, debuerunt hoc prius solido argumento aliquo confirmare quoad reprobationem daemonum, quam inde de hominum reprobatione consequentias inferre.
